question: A stakeholder wants to send an entire year of raw customer support transcripts, well beyond the model's context window, in a single request and asks why this fails. How should this limitation be explained?
options: A) Explain that Claude rejects large inputs purely as a cost-control step, and the limit lifts once the account tier is upgraded.
B) Explain that the failure means the account is rate-limited and will refuse further requests for the next 24 hours.
C) Explain that transcripts must always be converted into images before Claude will process any amount of text content.
D) Explain that each model has a maximum context window, so transcripts must be chunked, summarized, or retrieved selectively.
correct_answers: D) Explain that each model has a maximum context window, so transcripts must be chunked, summarized, or retrieved selectively.
explanations: Incorrect. The context window is a technical limit on how much input the model can process at once, not simply a billing lever tied to account tier.
Incorrect. Exceeding the context window is a distinct failure from rate limiting and does not imply a 24-hour account block.
Incorrect. Text does not need to be converted to images to be processed; this misrepresents how context limits work.
Correct. Every model has a fixed context window, so inputs that exceed it must be broken into chunks, summarized, or narrowed via retrieval rather than sent in one request.
